findings.message: The cited problem quantifies over every integer k ≠ 1; its discussion explicitly includes k = -1. Lean instead infers k : ℕ and assumes k > 1, so the theorem omits all negative k as well as k = 0 and formalises a strictly weaker problem.
findings.suggestion: Quantify over integers while retaining natural n, for example: `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k : ℤ), k ≠ 1 → { n : ℕ | 2 ^ n ≡ k [ZMOD n] }.Infinite`. This candidate elaborates successfully.
